title: Chapter 680
paragraphs: Chapter 680
Episode 173. Chasing the Sword (5)

Red pillars were shooting up from the seabed. The beams from the Graveyard Giants were dense, making them difficult to dodge, but the two managed to change direction by spreading their magic and aura while descending.
Like people who have been in sync for a long time, no more words were needed. Jin and Valeria moved as if they were one body, looking out for each other's safety.
Jin, thanks to his past life's memories, knew most of her combat style, but Valeria didn't.
Even so, Jin also felt a strange feeling when he fought with Valeria.
'Unlike me, the master doesn't know me well in this life, but we always get along well.'
'Fighting with Jin always feels strangely stable...'
The two, heading for the center of the enemy, were not yet seriously hit, but the situation above was already chaotic.
The Vamel Alliance had not been harmed thanks to Quikantel's evasion, but the problem was that there were too many of the Zipfel, Kinzelo, and Sword Garden's pursuit force.

Fish that are small enough to escape the net, and fish that can't. That was the state of the Vamel Alliance and the remaining forces. Only Quikantel, with the protection of those on his back, could easily avoid the beams.
The powerhouses of each faction strived to minimize ally damage, but the power of the Graveyard Giants was far beyond common sense.
If each Graveyard Giant had transcendental power, Jin wouldn't even think about fighting them.
No matter how strong, a weapon without a self has its limits.
Huaaak-!
Along with the red beams, large spear-like trees flew in from all directions. At a speed that was unimaginable considering their size and weight.
Jin didn't deliberately dodge the first spear to arrive, but instead hit it with his sword as a test, and his wrist felt really stiff.
'Attacks that are heavy but have no tricks or depth.'
Repetitive patterns like a machine reacting to a certain situation.
However, their numbers were so great that the array naturally became complex, but Jin was able to land on the seabed by fending off their spears without trouble.
As soon as the two touched the ground, the defensive equipment attached to the buildings all activated at once and targeted Jin.
'Is this an automatic responsive magic cannon, like the one made by Amelia?'
The magic cannon didn't identify allies. It just fired in Jin's direction, even if the Graveyard Giants were in the way.
But the cannon fire was reflected off like light off a mirror. The shots pinged off the bodies of the Graveyard Giants, making a noise that didn't match their power.
Most escaped into the sky or bounced off the sea wall, but there were still so many that many shots threatened Jin and Valeria's path.
'This will be a bit tiring.'
Just as that thought crossed his mind,
Valeria tapped the ground once with her silver pine staff. Then, a massive magic circle formed, flowing like water along a groove.
"It's not a shield."
"I'm going to twist the flow of the reflecting cannons. So, you just focus on destroying the Graveyard Giants."

The magic spreading from the magic circle began to inscribe runes into the air. Around a thousand runes fixed themselves in the air, each maintaining a distance of about five steps apart. The cannons couldn't easily pass between them and got caught.
Moreover, the cannons that got caught never reached the two. It seemed as if the cannons were completely unaware of the certain radius within which the two were moving.
'The size of the magic is much smaller than the destructive power of the cannons... is this possible?'
It's like a master diverting a novice's attack with much less power. Valeria was doing with magic what was usually seen in the fights of warriors.
'Probably, she also survived through such marvels from Rune Tia.'
Jin was again shocked by his master's magic.
"Understood."
Phzzzzt-!
Sigmund held a thick bolt of lightning.
Then, Jin, with his power infused, cut the ankle of the Graveyard Giant blocking his path. The blade didn't slide in smoothly.
Meaning it didn't cut.
Instead, with a dull sound, a portion of the ankle shattered and broke apart, which Jin thought was sufficient.
'If I swing with all my might, it's not that I can't cut...'
But to do that, he would have to focus highly every time he swung. There was no need to fight so inefficiently.
Crack!
With the blade lodged in, he exploded the lightning, and the Graveyard Giant's ankle shattered. It was a bit messy to consider as a cut by a warrior of Jin's caliber, but the effect was certain.
"Guaaaah...!"
At the moment the Graveyard Giant, whose ankle had exploded, knelt down to regain balance, Jin, who had leapt, stabbed the creature's head with his sword while climbing its body.
Before the fragments mixed with lightning even fell to the ground as the head burst apart, Jin, descending like lightning, fended off the spears flying at Valeria.
It was as if lightning was stomping on and crushing the spears. Jin was so small compared to the Graveyard Giants that he looked minuscule, but his presence was far more than all the giants combined.
'If it had been my father, he wouldn't have had to concentrate. He would naturally have disassembled these creatures.'
His brow briefly furrowed at the sudden thought of his father.
"You seem to have the luxury to have other thoughts. Every moment here is a matter of life and death for us."
"I'll try to focus more."
Actually, just as Valeria had twisted the trajectory of all the magic cannons, Jin could also ensure she was never hurt. As many Graveyard Giants as she wanted.
Despite knowing this, Valeria still spoke redundantly. Jin was slightly surprised that she would make such pointless comments to him.
A pleasant battle.

Regardless of the situation, their hearts were lightened every moment by the perfect harmony of their offense and defense. Whenever Jin swung his sword, somewhere on the Graveyard Giant would break, and whenever Valeria cast magic, their attacks would go awry.
No matter how many Graveyard Giants there were, it felt as though they could joyously break them all.
Already more than ten Graveyard Giants had been destroyed. In the meantime, new Graveyard Giants were forming, but luckily, their formation was not faster than the two could handle.
Also, the rate at which new Graveyard Giants were appearing was gradually slowing. Jin expected that no more would be created once a certain number was reached.
"Jin."
"Why?"
"Normally, these weapons stop operating when the object they're guarding disappears."
"Are you saying there might be remnants of a forgotten god somewhere in this grave?"
"It could be, or... the god itself could still be around."
"Could the person presumed to be a surviving old Runcandel be a god?"

"Since I can't use record magic right now, we can't confirm until we meet him. Even if we look at the records, there won't be many areas that I can know at my current level. Also, their movements seem too simple, even if they are simple."
At Valeria's words, Jin suddenly felt that the movement of the Graveyard Giants was strange. It seemed as if there was some sort of intention.
"Listening to you, it doesn't seem like the Graveyard Giants are just moving to get rid of the intruders."
Each one was so huge, and because they were just breaking them as they could, worried about friendly damage, they hadn't recognized it until now.
"The formation they're taking is not encircling us, Valeria. It just seemed like we were being pressured naturally because of their size."
Jin and Valeria began to closely observe the overall movement of the Graveyard Giants as they passed between their legs.
Firstly, not all Graveyard Giants were attacking Jin and Valeria. Some Graveyard Giants stood still, staring at the ground, while others were digging the earth.
If they're not broken, there's only one reason to dig the ground.
"They're trying to find something."

"The Graveyard Giants exploring underground have a more sophisticated form than the others. Jin, if my guess is correct, this is an ancient unsealing method. They're trying to find the core of a seal buried somewhere here."
"What happens after they find the core?"

"All the power of the Graveyard Giants will be connected to the core, and the seal will likely be broken. The fact that the sword has been flying for so long could have been part of the process of finding the hidden core."
"So, if we destroy all of them, it means that the sealed entity cannot awaken."
Valeria nodded.
"The choice is yours."
Awakening from the seal is an old Runcandel, presumed to be a god or a god-like entity.
There was no guarantee that whoever it was would be friendly to them. It was much more likely that they would be hostile.
Or beyond just being hostile, it was also possible that they might be filled with resentment and hatred, like Padler.
"Let's wake them up."
However, Jin didn't even hesitate.
If they destroy all the Graveyard Giants right now, they and their companions will be safe, but a piece of the history of the old Runcandel will be lost forever.
From then on, the two switched to full defensive mode. The Graveyard Giants continued to attack, but as the two did not fight back, the intensity gradually diminished.
About ten minutes later, the Graveyard Giants stopped attacking them. However, the attacks toward the sky did not stop.
"The Graveyard Giants aren't attacking you and Aria. You must have found some clue. We just have to keep dodging and blocking!"
As a result, the sky turned into a battlefield, but it didn't have much impact on their companions.
From the beginning, the Vamel Alliance never counterattacked after the Graveyard Giants woke up.

On the other hand, since Zipfel and Kinzelo, and the Sword's Garden, were always fighting, the Graveyard Giants did not even recognize the Quikantel group as enemies from a certain point. The reason they still had to dodge the red beam was simply because their allies overlapped with the detected enemies.
"I nearly committed a great rudeness to our ancestor who is waking up after a thousand years."
After about ten more minutes, one of the Graveyard Giants flashed its eye and began to vibrate. Coincidentally, it was the Graveyard Giant right in front of Jin and Valeria.
"GROOOOOOOOOAR!"
As that Graveyard Giant roared, the other giants also lit up their eyes and shook their bodies, which seemed to be a process of pouring power into the core of the seal.
The first roaring Graveyard Giant finally raised the two hands that had been stirring under the sea.
In its hand was a sphere shining like a small sun, and Jin and Valeria could see the power of the Graveyard Giants concentrating there all at once.
"Pray that what awakens is something we can handle, Jin."
